config.title: Streams

intro.title: Streams
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple file processing application that reads a large text file and writes a transformed version to a new file. You will learn the core concept of streams in Node.js, which allow you to handle data in chunks efficiently without loading entire files into memory. The main technologies involved are the built-in Node.js 'fs' module and its 'createReadStream' and 'createWriteStream' methods. By the end, you'll understand how to use readable and writable streams to process data piece by piece, making your applications more performant and scalable.
intro.usecase: Streams are fundamental in Node.js for handling large files and data flows efficiently, such as when processing video uploads on platforms like YouTube or Netflix, where files are too large to load entirely into memory. They enable real-time data processing in applications like log monitoring tools or financial trading platforms, where data arrives continuously and needs immediate analysis. Streams also power features like live chat in messaging apps, where messages are transmitted and displayed as they're received without waiting for complete transmission. As a developer, you'll use streams to build scalable applications that handle I/O operations without blocking the event loop, crucial for high-performance web servers and data processing pipelines.

objectives: Implement a readable stream to read data from a file
Construct a writable stream to write data to a file
Configure a transform stream to modify data during processing
Integrate multiple streams using pipe() for data flow
Manipulate stream events to handle data, end, and error scenarios
Initialize a duplex stream for bidirectional data communication
Control stream flow using pause() and resume() methods

steps.title: Import the fs module
steps.instruction: Import the Node.js fs module using require() so you can work with file streams.
steps.hint: Use the require() function to import the built-in 'fs' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing another built-in module
const http = require('http');
steps.expectedOutcome: The fs module is imported and ready to use for file operations.
successCriteria: The fs module is imported using require('fs').
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using require('fs') exactly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The fs module isn't imported correctly. Use require('fs') to import the file system module.

steps.title: Create a readable stream
steps.instruction: Create a readable stream using fs.createReadStream() with the file path './data.txt' and assign it to a variable named 'readStream'.
steps.hint: Use the fs module you imported in the previous step. The createReadStream method takes a file path as its first argument.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a readable stream for a file
const readStream = fs.createReadStream('./example.txt');
steps.expectedOutcome: A readable stream object will be created that can read data from the specified file.
successCriteria: A variable named 'readStream' is declared and assigned the result of fs.createReadStream('./data.txt').
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using fs.createReadStream() with the exact file path './data.txt' and assigning it to a variable named 'readStream'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to create a readable stream using the fs module's createReadStream method with the file path './data.txt'.

steps.title: Handle data events from the readable stream
steps.instruction: Add a 'data' event listener to the readable stream that logs each chunk to the console.
steps.hint: Use the .on() method on the stream object with 'data' as the event name and a callback function that receives the chunk.
steps.expectedOutcome: The stream will start emitting data events, and each chunk will be logged to the console as it arrives.
successCriteria: A 'data' event listener is attached to readableStream that logs each chunk.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the listener is attached to readableStream and logs the chunk parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using .on('data', callback) on the readableStream and the callback logs the chunk.

steps.title: Handle end events from the readable stream
steps.instruction: Add an 'end' event listener to the readableStream to log a message when the stream finishes reading the file.
steps.hint: Use readableStream.on('end', callback) where the callback is a function that logs a completion message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The readable stream will log a completion message when it finishes reading the file.
successCriteria: An 'end' event listener is added to readableStream that logs a message when the stream ends.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the 'end' event listener to readableStream with a callback that logs a message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The 'end' event listener is missing or incorrect. Use readableStream.on('end', callback) to handle when the stream finishes.

steps.title: Handle error events from the readable stream
steps.instruction: Add an 'error' event listener to the readable stream to handle errors by logging the error message to the console.
steps.hint: Use readableStream.on('error', callback) with a callback that takes an error parameter and logs it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The readable stream now has an error event listener that logs error messages.
successCriteria: An 'error' event listener is added to readableStream that logs the error message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're adding an 'error' event listener to readableStream that logs the error message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The error event listener is missing or incorrect. Try adding readableStream.on('error', callback) with a callback that logs the error.

steps.title: Create a writable stream
steps.instruction: Create a writable stream using fs.createWriteStream() with the file path './output.txt'.
steps.hint: Use the same fs module you imported earlier. Call createWriteStream with a string path.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a writable stream for a file
const writableStream = fs.createWriteStream('./log.txt');
steps.expectedOutcome: A writable stream variable is created, ready to write data to output.txt.
successCriteria: A writable stream is created using fs.createWriteStream() with the correct file path.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using fs.createWriteStream() with the file path './output.txt'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to create a writable stream using fs.createWriteStream('./output.txt').

steps.title: Pipe readable stream to writable stream
steps.instruction: Pipe the readable stream to the writable stream using the pipe() method.
steps.hint: Call the pipe() method on the readableStream and pass the writableStream as an argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: The readable stream will automatically transfer data to the writable stream when the code runs.
successCriteria: The pipe() method is called on readableStream with writableStream as the argument.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling pipe() on the readableStream and passing the writableStream as an argument.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't seem to be the correct way to pipe streams. Remember to use the pipe() method on the readable stream with the writable stream as an argument.

steps.title: Handle finish events from the writable stream
steps.instruction: Add a 'finish' event listener to the writable stream to log a completion message.
steps.hint: Use the .on() method on the writable stream with the event name 'finish' and a callback function that logs a message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The writable stream will log a message when it has finished writing all data from the readable stream.
successCriteria: A 'finish' event listener is added to the writable stream with a callback that logs a completion message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the event listener is attached to the writable stream and logs a message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The 'finish' event listener is missing or incorrect. Try adding .on('finish', callback) to the writable stream.

steps.instruction: Create a transform stream using the stream.Transform class. Name it 'transformStream'.
steps.hint: You'll need to import the 'stream' module and create a new instance of Transform.

successCriteria: The transform stream is created using the stream.Transform class and assigned to a variable named 'transformStream'.

steps.instruction: Inside the transform stream you created, implement the _transform method to convert incoming data chunks to uppercase.
steps.hint: The _transform method receives three parameters: chunk, encoding, and callback. Use chunk.toString().toUpperCase() to transform the data, then call callback(null, transformedData).

successCriteria: The transform stream has a _transform method that converts chunk data to uppercase and calls the callback with the transformed data.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
